title: SVT with aberrancy (AVNRT with right bundle branch block)
summary: A supraventricular tachycardia conducted with a bundle branch block looks like a wide-complex tachycardia.

events.label: Sinus beat
events.caption: This patient has a right bundle branch block, so even sinus beats have a wide QRS.
events.ecg: A wide QRS with a sinus P wave.

events.label: AVNRT starts
events.caption: A premature atrial beat starts AV nodal reentry exactly as in ordinary AVNRT: down the slow pathway, back up the fast one.
events.ecg: An early P wave, then a regular tachycardia.

events.label: Wide-complex tachycardia
events.caption: The circuit is entirely supraventricular, but every impulse is conducted with the same bundle branch block, so the QRS is wide.
events.ecg: A regular wide-complex tachycardia that looks like ventricular tachycardia.

events.label: The clue
events.caption: The QRS is the same shape as in sinus rhythm. VT usually looks different from the patient's own conducted beats.
events.ecg: The tachycardia QRS matches the sinus-rhythm QRS.

teaching_points: Aberrancy: a supraventricular tachycardia conducted with a bundle branch block (existing or rate-related) gives a wide QRS.
Most wide-complex tachycardias are ventricular tachycardia, so treat it as VT unless proven otherwise.
A QRS identical to the patient's QRS in sinus rhythm supports SVT with aberrancy.
